findings.title: Cache deletion leaves the 'Last updated' status stale in the UI
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess (lines 42-46) only shows a toast and calls the parent's onSuccess (onChanged). Unlike disconnectMutation, it never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so the cacheUpdatedAt prop is not refreshed. After a successful 'Delete cached data', the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete item stays visible until something else refetches. Whether it refreshes depends on the parent's onChanged, which this component does not control. The PR's own test plan item 'Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately' would fail as written.

findings.title: Unused SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write on every cache refresh
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) on every refresh, including webhook-driven ones. This bumps updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, across all event types. The PR's own notes say the frontend reads CalendarCache.updatedAt and not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this extra UPDATE has no consumer. It also changes the meaning of an existing column that is now selected into UserWithCalendars and the user session selects. Remove it, or justify it with a real consumer.

findings.title: Existing CalendarCache rows are backfilled with the migration time as updatedAt
findings.body: Adding the column with DEFAULT NOW() sets updatedAt for every pre-existing cache row to the deployment time. Immediately after deploy, the 'Last updated' label shows the deploy time for all Google calendars, even when the cached data is weeks old. Nothing in the PR marks these rows as legacy or unknown, so the UI presents a misleading freshness value.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the migration body
findings.body: The Prisma-generated warning block says the required updatedAt column is added 'without a default value' and 'is not possible if the table is not empty'. The statement below adds the column with DEFAULT NOW(), so the warning is wrong for this migration and misleads reviewers about the migration's safety.

findings.title: Stale TODO says CalendarCache has no updatedAt column
findings.body: The comment says updatedAt 'doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table'. This PR adds that column in schema.prisma and the migration, so the comment is now false. It also misses the point that the new column is what the PR relies on for cacheUpdatedAt.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US instead of the user's locale
findings.body: The label text is translated with t(), but the timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...). Users with other locales see an English-format date inside a localized sentence. The locale from useLocale() should be used for formatting.

findings.title: No tests for the deleteCache ownership check or cache-status grouping
findings.body: The handler's only access control is the findFirst on {id, userId}. This PR adds no test that a user cannot delete another user's credential cache. The new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy/_max mapping and the connectedCalendarsHandler enrichment also have no tests. These are security-relevant and easy to regress.

findings.title: Unrelated dev:cron change swaps ts-node for an unpinned npx tsx call
findings.body: The dev:cron script changes from ts-node to npx tsx. This is unrelated to calendar cache. tsx is not declared in apps/web's dependencies or devDependencies, so npx fetches whatever tsx version the registry serves at run time, outside the lockfile. The change should be justified and the dependency declared, or reverted from this PR.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and breaks the update path on Linux
findings.body: The script uses BSD syntax sed -i '' -E ... . With GNU sed, the empty string is taken as the script and the expression as a filename, so the update fails whenever GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists in the env file. The script is not documented as macOS-only, and the failure is not caught.

findings.title: ENV_FILE path is relative to the working directory, not the script
findings.body: ENV_FILE="../.env" resolves against the caller's current directory. It points at the repo's .env only when run from scripts/. Run from the repo root, as the usual `./scripts/...` invocation suggests, it writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into a .env one directory above the repo. It should be resolved from the script's own location.
